docs.text: HardFOC board HAL Flux V1 HAL ¶ The software layer for the HardFOC Flux V1 valve control board. One Flux object gives your ESP32-S3 application eight solenoid valve channels, six proportional valve channels, analog inputs, temperatures, CAN, storage and a status LED, through a small set of managers that know the board's wiring. Quickstart Architecture Source on GitHub This repository ( hf-hal-flux-v1 ) turns the board into C++ objects. Your application does not touch GPIO numbers or SPI frames; it calls flux.valves , flux.adc , flux.temp . Valve control board Flux V1 HardFOC MCU ESP32-S3, dual core; ESP-IDF release/v5.5 Valve drivers MAX22200: 8 on/off solenoid channels (hit and hold) · TLE92466ED: 6 proportional channels (regulated current, PWM, dither); one SPI bus, 1 MHz Analog inputs ADS7952: 12 channels, 12 bit, 2.5 V reference, own SPI bus at 4 MHz · ESP32 ADC1: NTC thermistor and supply voltage Communication CAN 500 kbit/s (TWAI) · UART for a PyroScience FDO2 oxygen probe · USB Serial/JTAG (console, flashing) Power 24 V valve supply, needed only to drive valves; the board starts and logs from USB without it Status One WS2812 RGB LED Hardware · Pin map Flux V1 HAL, layer by layer Figure description and sources From top to bottom, each layer only calls the one under it. Your application asks the facade singleton for the managers. The managers (one per board function) own the hf-core handlers, which wrap one chip driver each; a manager may also use a driver directly. Drivers talk to hardware only through the interface classes of the internal interface wrap, whose ESP32 implementations sit on ESP-IDF. Every name in a band is read from the code: the managers from the facade's member references, the handlers, drivers and interface classes from the managers' and handlers' #include lines. Drawn from: lib/api/Flux.h Flux (manager references) ; lib/managers #includes ; lib/core/handlers #includes ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/hal-layers.py . What you get ¶ One Flux object that brings the board up in a fixed order and reports what failed ( Initialisation ). One manager per board function: valves, ADC, temperature, GPIO, LED, communication, storage ( Managers ). Valve channels by name ( ValveChannel::SOL_CH0 , PROP_CH0 ), whichever chip drives them ( ValveManager ). A pin map generated from the board's pin header, so the pages cannot disagree with the firmware ( Pin map ). Diagnostics for every manager: GetLastError() , health snapshots, DumpSystemStatistics() ( Errors and diagnostics ). Example apps for each manager, built by CI on every pull request ( Examples ). Where to go next ¶ Quickstart Install ESP-IDF, clone with submodules, build, flash and watch the first example. Bring-up and troubleshooting The first power-up, step by step, and what each start-up warning means. Hardware Buses, chips and the pin map, generated from the board's pin header. Architecture Layers, start-up order, ownership, threading and errors. Managers One page per manager: what it does, its API, an example and its pitfalls. Examples Every buildable app, generated from app_config.yml .

docs.text: Bring-up and troubleshooting ¶ How to bring a new Flux V1 board up one function at a time, and what to do when a step fails. Bring up a new board ¶ Work from the cheapest check to the most expensive, and do not connect valves until the steps before pass. Each app is built and flashed as in the quickstart ( ./scripts/flash_app.sh flash_monitor <app> Release from examples/esp32 ). USB only, no valve supply. Flash flux_api_test . The start-up table must show OK for NVS, Comms and GPIO: they are required, and EnsureInitialized() returns false without them. WARN on Valves is expected here. GPIO and analog inputs. Flash gpio_adc_test ; every test must pass. The ESP32 ADC channels (NTC, supply voltage) answer even without the ADS7952; the ADC_ADS7952_* channels exist only when the ADS7952 answers on its SPI bus. LED and temperatures. Flash led_temp_test ; every test must pass. The LED shows the OK, warning and error status colours, and the ESP32 internal sensor and the NTC read within range. Valve supply, no valves. Connect the 24 V valve supply and flash flux_api_test again. Valves must now be OK ; flux.valves.GetSystemDiagnostics(...) reports max22200_initialized and tle92466_initialized . One valve. Connect one solenoid to SOL_CH0 and flash valve_cycling_test . Then the proportional channels, one at a time. Valve current A solenoid channel drives the current you configure ( ConfigureSolenoidCdr hit and hold, in mA) as soon as it is enabled. Check the valve's rating before step 5; the MAX22200 full scale on this board is 1000 mA. Build ¶ Symptom Cause Fix build_app.sh: No such file or directory The examples/esp32/scripts submodule is missing git submodule update --init --recursive CMake cannot find lib/core/... headers lib/core or its nested submodules are missing Same as above, from the repository root APP_TYPE not defined idf.py build was run directly Build through ./scripts/build_app.sh <app> <type> No supported board variant defined! Building hf-core without the HAL's CMake Build through this repository; its CMakeLists.txt defines HARDFOC_BOARD_FLUX_V1 Wrong target errors An old build folder for another target Delete the app's build folder; the target is esp32s3 Start-up ¶ Symptom Cause Fix NVS ... FAIL , EnsureInitialized() returns false NVS partition full or written by another firmware Erase flash once: idf.py -p PORT erase-flash (this erases everything) Valves WARN Neither valve driver answered Check the 24 V valve supply and the valve SPI wiring; the log says which chip failed Only one valve chip works The other chip failed its own start-up flux.valves.GetSystemDiagnostics(...) shows max22200_initialized / tle92466_initialized ; the other chip's channels return VALVE_ERR_DRIVER_NOT_AVAILABLE ADC WARN or no ADC_ADS7952_* channels The ADS7952 did not answer on the ADC SPI bus Check the ADC SPI pins on the pin map ; the ESP32 ADC channels still work No MCP9700_THERMISTOR Needs a working ADS7952 channel 8 Fix the ADS7952 first Valves ¶ Symptom Cause Fix EnableChannel() succeeds but the valve does not move Valve supply off, or the channel was never configured Check 24 V; call ConfigureSolenoidCdr/Vdr or SetProportionalCurrent first VALVE_ERR_CHANNEL_TYPE_MISMATCH A solenoid call on a PROP_CH* channel or the reverse Use the call for the channel's chip (see ValveManager ) Proportional current reads 0 Feedback frozen or supply under-voltage Start-up clears the freeze; check GetProportionalFaults() for a supply fault LED and GPIO ¶ Symptom Cause Fix LED animation stuck on the first frame Nobody calls UpdateAnimation() Call it from a periodic task GPIO_ERR_PIN_NOT_FOUND Typo, or the pin is not a GPIO-category pin Use the exact name from the pin map A fault input always reads the same The pin is still an output SetDirection(name, HF_GPIO_DIRECTION_INPUT) ; ValveManager does this for the two fault pins Still stuck ¶ Run flux_api_test and read its log top to bottom: it initialises each manager and prints what it found. Then call Flux::GetInstance().DumpSystemStatistics() from your own code to log every manager's state.

docs.text: Quickstart ¶ This page takes you from nothing to a Flux V1 board printing its start-up log. Each step says how to tell that it worked. Plan on half an hour, most of it the ESP-IDF download. What you need ¶ Item Notes A Flux V1 board Any revision with the ESP32-S3 module USB cable Data-capable; the board enumerates as a USB serial / JTAG device A 24 V valve supply Only for driving valves. The board starts and logs without it Linux, macOS or Windows (WSL2) The build scripts are Bash 1. Install ESP-IDF ¶ The examples target esp32s3 and build with ESP-IDF release/v5.5 (both read from examples/esp32/app_config.yml , which CI uses too). mkdir -p ~/esp && cd ~/esp git clone -b release/v5.5 --recursive https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf.git cd esp-idf && ./install.sh esp32s3 . ./export.sh It worked if idf.py --version prints a v5.5 version. Run . ~/esp/esp-idf/export.sh in every new terminal. 2. Clone with submodules ¶ The HAL pulls the shared core ( lib/core : handlers, drivers, the pin map) and the build scripts as git submodules. git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-hal-flux-v1.git cd hf-hal-flux-v1 If you already cloned without submodules: git submodule update --init --recursive It worked if ls lib/core/handlers lists handler folders and ls examples/esp32/scripts shows build_app.sh . One submodule is private docs/hf-development-handbook is a private repository and is marked update = none , so the recursive update skips it. You do not need it to build. 3. Build an example ¶ Every example is an "app" selected by name. Start with flux_api_test , the default app, which initialises the whole HAL and checks each manager. cd examples/esp32 ./scripts/build_app.sh list # every app name ./scripts/build_app.sh flux_api_test Release # build one It worked if the script ends with a successful link and a build folder named after the app, the build type and the target appears under examples/esp32/ . 4. Flash and monitor ¶ Connect the board over USB, then: ./scripts/flash_app.sh flash_monitor flux_api_test Release Set ESPPORT first if more than one serial port is present (for example export ESPPORT=/dev/ttyACM0 ). Leave the monitor with Ctrl + ] . It worked if the log shows the Flux start-up table: one row per manager (NVS, Comms, GPIO, Valves, ADC, LEDs, Temp) with OK , WARN or FAIL , then Flux API initialized in ... ms . WARN on Valves or ADC is normal without the valve supply or with unfitted parts; see Initialisation . 5. Use the HAL in your own code ¶ #include "api/Flux.h" #include "managers/ValveManager.h" extern "C" void app_main () { auto & flux = Flux :: GetInstance (); if ( ! flux . EnsureInitialized ()) { return ; // NVS, comms or GPIO failed: nothing below can work } if ( flux . valves . IsInitialized ()) { ( void ) flux . valves . ConfigureSolenoidCdr ( ValveChannel :: SOL_CH0 , 800 , 300 , 20.0f ); ( void ) flux . valves . EnableChannel ( ValveChannel :: SOL_CH0 ); } } Next ¶ Architecture explains the layers under Flux . Examples lists every app and what it shows. Bring-up and troubleshooting covers a new board and the common first-day problems.

docs.text: Roadmap ¶ Where the Flux V1 HAL is going, and the known gaps on the way. Items in "next" come from the code as it is today; nothing here is a promise of a date. Now ¶ One Flux facade and seven managers covering every chip on the board ( Managers ). Pin map, examples catalogue and figures generated from the code, checked in CI ( Testing and CI ). Builds for the ESP32-S3 with ESP-IDF release/v5.5. Next: close the known gaps ¶ Gap Where Why it matters ValveManager and AdcManager never record their last error ValveManager.cpp , AdcManager.cpp The health snapshot reports them healthy after a failed call ( Errors ) Flux::Shutdown() skips ValveManager Flux.cpp Valves stay as they were on shutdown ( Initialisation ) Flux::GetSystemWarnings() is always empty Flux.h Nothing calls the internal AddSystemWarning() GPIO pins all start as outputs GpioManager.cpp Fault inputs are outputs until ValveManager reconfigures them No host unit tests - Logic such as channel resolution and error mapping is only tested on hardware ESP-IDF calls in the facade and LED manager Flux.cpp , LedManager.* Leaks across the MCU boundary ( ADR 0001 ) Later: new transports and MCUs ¶ CAN protocols. The HAL already builds the hf-core CANopen helpers ( HF_CORE_ENABLE_UTILS_CANOPEN in CMakeLists.txt ) and exposes the CAN bus as BaseCan* through CommChannelsManager::GetCanBus() . A CANopen device profile for Flux would sit above that, in the application, without changing the managers. The Vortex V1 board is getting the first HardFOC CANopen node, and its design will be reused here where it fits. Another MCU and CAN FD. The interface-wrap boundary in ADR 0001 is what a port to an STM32 with CAN FD would use: new Base* implementations created by the managers, a pin map for the new board, and the same handlers and application code above.

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ What runs on a pull request, what each check means, and how to run it on your machine first. All workflows are in .github/workflows ; most call reusable workflows in hf-general-ci-tools or hf-espidf-ci-tools . Preview the site ¶ python3 -m pip install "git+https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-general-ci-tools@v1#subdirectory=packages/hardfoc-mkdocs-theme" mkdocs serve Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 . mkdocs build --strict is what CI runs: a broken link, a missing image or an image without alt text fails it. Write a page ¶ Say what the page is for in its first sentence, then answer it. Prefer short sections, tables and numbered steps. Link to code with a relative path, as GitHub resolves it ( ../lib/api/Foo.h ); the site rewrites the link to the file on GitHub at the commit that was built. Link to the API reference under api/ ( ../api-reference.md explains it); the link is checked on the built site, after the API is merged. Use admonitions ( !!! note , !!! warning ) for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration. A new folder gets an index.md ; docs/.nav.yml orders the top tabs. Add a figure ¶ A figure is a Python module in docs/diagrams/figures/ . It extracts its facts from the code in data() , lists the files they come from in "sources" , and lays them out in build(data) with figkit ( from hardfoc_mkdocs_theme.figkit import Fig ). Light and dark are the same layout, so they cannot drift apart. Add a generated table ¶ A generator is a module in tools/docs/generators/ with a REGIONS dict from a region name to a function that returns Markdown. Mark the region on a page and run hardfoc-docs gen ; CI runs it with --check : <!-- generated: my-table --> <!-- /generated --> Record a decision ¶ Copy the ADR template to the next number in docs/adr/ and add it to the table in Decisions .

docs.text: ADR 0001: Keep the MCU behind the interface wrap; only managers know the board ¶ Status Accepted (records the current design) Date 2026-11-01 Context ¶ HardFOC boards share chips (the WS2812 LED, NTC sensors, CAN) and a common core ( hf-core : handlers, drivers, interface wrap). Flux V1 runs on an ESP32-S3 today. Future boards are expected on other MCUs, in particular an STM32 with CAN FD, and the same valve and sensor code should move with them. Options ¶ Write the HAL directly against ESP-IDF. Fast to start; every manager and handler would need rewriting for another MCU. Put the MCU behind interface classes and keep board knowledge in one layer. Chip drivers and handlers use only BaseSpi , BaseGpio , BaseAdc , BaseCan , BaseUart , BaseNvs , BaseTemperature ; the managers are the only code that knows which chip is on which pin of which board. Decision ¶ Option 2. The boundary is: Drivers and handlers (in hf-core ) depend only on the Base* interface classes. The ESP32 implementations ( EspSpiBus , EspGpio , EspAdc , EspCan , EspUart , EspNvs , EspTemperature ) are named in exactly the managers that create buses and peripherals: CommChannelsManager , GpioManager , AdcManager , NvsManager , TemperatureManager . The generated manager map lists them, read from the #include lines. Board wiring lives in the per-board pin map in hf-pincfg ( ADR 0003 ). Task placement uses logical core indices ( FluxCpuAffinity.h ), not vendor core names. Consequences ¶ A port to another MCU replaces the Esp* construction in those managers (with Stm* or other implementations of the same interfaces) and adds a pin map; handlers, drivers and application code above the managers stay. CAN FD fits the same seam: a future FD-capable BaseCan implementation (larger frames, data-phase bit timing) is created by CommChannelsManager instead of EspCan ; code that only sees BaseCan* keeps working, and code that wants FD frames checks the port's capabilities. Known leaks across the boundary today, to fix before a port: Flux.cpp calls ESP-IDF directly for reset reason, heap size and restart ( esp_reset_reason() , heap_caps_* , esp_restart() ); LedManager uses the ESP-IDF RMT WS2812 driver and gpio_num_t ; the valve and ADC SPI host numbers in CommChannelsManager.cpp are ESP32 values.

docs.text: ADR 0002: Allocate once at start-up; fixed tables sized from the pin map ¶ Status Accepted (records the current design, with the exceptions listed) Date 2026-11-01 Context ¶ The board runs for long periods controlling valves. Heap fragmentation or an allocation failure in the middle of a control loop is hard to diagnose and can leave a valve in the wrong state. On the other hand the number of chips that actually answer is only known at start-up, and some objects (ESP-IDF drivers) are easiest to create on the heap. Options ¶ Everything static. No heap at all; every driver object a member. Rigid, and some driver classes are not designed for it. Allocate once at start-up, never after. Tables with a known size are fixed arrays; objects whose existence depends on start-up results are created on the heap during EnsureInitialized() and kept for the program's life. Allocate freely. Simple, and the problems above. Decision ¶ Option 2: Tables with a compile-time count are std::array , sized from the pin map or a sentinel enum: GpioManager::entries_ ( HF_FUNCTIONAL_GPIO_COUNT ), AdcManager::entries_ ( HF_FUNCTIONAL_ADC_COUNT ), ValveManager::channel_states_ ( ValveChannel::CHANNEL_COUNT ), the SPI device tables ( SpiDeviceId::DEVICE_COUNT ), the facade's diagnostics arrays ( kFluxManagerCount ). Bus objects, handlers and drivers are held in std::unique_ptr , created during the owning manager's initialisation, mostly with hf::utils::make_unique_nothrow so a failed allocation is a logged initialisation failure rather than an abort. No manager allocates in its read, write or channel calls. Consequences ¶ After Flux::EnsureInitialized() the valve, ADC, temperature, GPIO and LED paths do not touch the heap. GetFreeHeapBytes() after start-up is a useful, stable number to log. Where this is not strictly true today: CommChannelsManager::AcquireUart() creates a UART on the first call for a port, whenever the application makes it. Acquire UARTs during your own start-up. GpioManager and LedManager use std::make_unique (not the no-throw variant) for their pin and LED objects. Allocations inside ESP-IDF and the chip drivers are not covered by this decision.

docs.text: ADR 0003: The hf-pincfg X-macro table is the single source of pin truth ¶ Status Accepted (records the current design) Date 2026-11-01 Context ¶ A pin number written in more than one place drifts: the schematic changes, one copy is updated, another is not, and the board misbehaves in a way no compiler catches. Pin numbers used to be repeated in this repository's README, in examples and in docs. Options ¶ Pins as constants in each manager. Simple; every manager and every document repeats them. One table per board, used by the code and by the docs. The board's functional pin map in hf-pincfg ( hf_functional_pin_config_flux_v1.hpp ), written as X-macro rows; everything else reads it. Decision ¶ Option 2: Each row of HF_FUNCTIONAL_GPIO_PIN_LIST / HF_FUNCTIONAL_ADC_CHANNEL_LIST names a function, its chip, pin, polarity, pull, drive and current. The same rows generate the enums, name tables and mapping arrays. The managers register from the generated arrays: GpioManager creates a GPIO for each GPIO-category row, AdcManager a channel for each ADC row, CommChannelsManager and LedManager look up their pins with GetGpioMapping() . No manager writes a GPIO number. The pin map page and the board figure are generated from the same rows ( hardfoc-docs gen , hardfoc-docs figures ), and CI fails if they are stale. Consequences ¶ Changing a pin is one edit in hf-pincfg , a submodule bump here, and a docs rebuild. The pin map is shared by all HardFOC boards' HALs through hf-pincfg ; the board is chosen at build time with HARDFOC_BOARD_FLUX_V1 (set in this repository's CMakeLists.txt ). Hand-written comments in the header (the GPIO allocation list at the top) are not checked and can drift from the rows; the rows win.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the Flux V1 HAL is put together. The short version: your code talks to one object, Flux ; Flux holds one manager per board function; managers own hf-core handlers; handlers wrap chip drivers; drivers reach the hardware only through the interface classes of the internal interface wrap, which sit on ESP-IDF. Flux V1 HAL, layer by layer Figure description and sources From top to bottom, each layer only calls the one under it. Your application asks the facade singleton for the managers. The managers (one per board function) own the hf-core handlers, which wrap one chip driver each; a manager may also use a driver directly. Drivers talk to hardware only through the interface classes of the internal interface wrap, whose ESP32 implementations sit on ESP-IDF. Every name in a band is read from the code: the managers from the facade's member references, the handlers, drivers and interface classes from the managers' and handlers' #include lines. Drawn from: lib/api/Flux.h Flux (manager references) ; lib/managers #includes ; lib/core/handlers #includes ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/hal-layers.py . The layers ¶ Layer Where What it does You use it when Application your project, examples/esp32 Tasks, control loops, protocols Always Facade lib/api/Flux.h One singleton; brings the managers up in order; system diagnostics Always: Flux::GetInstance() Managers lib/managers One per board function (valves, ADC, temperature, ...); know the board's wiring from the pin map Almost always: flux.valves , flux.adc , ... hf-core handlers lib/core/handlers Wrap one chip driver each and adapt it to the interface classes Rarely; for chip features a manager does not expose Chip drivers lib/core/hf-core-drivers/external Register-level drivers, one repository per chip Almost never from application code Interface wrap lib/core/hf-core-drivers/internal/hf-internal-interface-wrap BaseSpi , BaseGpio , BaseAdc , ... and their ESP32 implementations ( EspSpi , EspGpio , ...) When porting to another MCU The rule that holds the design together: a layer only calls the layer below it. The managers are the only code that knows Flux V1 exists; handlers and drivers are shared with other HardFOC boards. Why the line is drawn there is recorded in ADR 0001 . Read on ¶ Initialisation : the order the managers come up and what happens when one fails. Ownership : which manager creates which handler, and how memory is allocated. Threading : which calls are safe from several tasks. Errors and diagnostics : error enums, GetLastError() , health snapshots.

docs.text: Errors and diagnostics ¶ The HAL does not throw. Every call is noexcept and reports failure through its return value. This page lists the error types, where to read the last error, and the system-level diagnostics. Rules of thumb ¶ Check the return value. Most methods are [[nodiscard]] ; the compiler warns if you drop a result. docs.text: Initialisation ¶ Flux::EnsureInitialized() brings every manager up, one at a time, in a fixed order. Call it once, early in app_main() , before you touch any manager. Flux::EnsureInitialized() Figure description and sources Left to right, then the second row. The facade initialises the managers one at a time, in the order of the calls in its init function. The first group is required: if any of them fails, EnsureInitialized() returns false and the application should not continue. The second group is best effort: a failure there is logged as a warning, the manager stays unavailable and the system reports itself as degraded, so a bench with only some chips fitted still comes up. The order and the required / best-effort split are read from the init function, which returns false only in the required branches. Drawn from: lib/api/Flux.cpp Flux::InitializeAllComponents ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/init-order.py . The order ¶ From Flux.cpp ( Flux::InitializeAllComponents ); do not edit. Step Manager Member If it fails 1 NvsManager flux.nvs initialisation fails ( EnsureInitialized() returns false) 2 CommChannelsManager flux.comms initialisation fails ( EnsureInitialized() returns false) 3 GpioManager flux.gpio initialisation fails ( EnsureInitialized() returns false) 4 ValveManager flux.valves warning; the system runs degraded 5 AdcManager flux.adc warning; the system runs degraded 6 LedManager flux.leds warning; the system runs degraded 7 TemperatureManager flux.temp warning; the system runs degraded The order follows the dependencies: storage first, so configuration and calibration are available early; then the buses; then the GPIO pins the valve drivers need; then the managers that use them. TemperatureManager comes after AdcManager because the NTC and MCP9700 sensors are read through ADC channels. What happens when a step fails ¶ Required steps (NVS, comms, GPIO). If one fails, EnsureInitialized() logs the failure, stops and returns false . IsInitialized() stays false , and calling EnsureInitialized() again retries from the start. Best-effort steps (valves, ADC, LEDs, temperature). A failure is logged as a WARN row in the start-up table and the manager stays unavailable; the remaining steps still run and EnsureInitialized() returns true . Check flux.valves.IsInitialized() (or the diagnostics ) before relying on a best-effort manager. This lets a bench with only some chips fitted, or with the 24 V valve supply off, still come up and log. Inside a best-effort manager the same idea repeats. ValveManager tries the TLE92466ED and the MAX22200 separately and succeeds if either works; TemperatureManager succeeds if any one of its three sensors works; AdcManager succeeds if any channel registered. Each logs which parts are missing. Calling a manager directly ¶ Every manager also has its own EnsureInitialized() , and the managers that depend on others call those first (for example ValveManager calls CommChannelsManager and GpioManager ). So code that uses one manager on its own works, but going through Flux::EnsureInitialized() gives you the logged start-up table and the system diagnostics. Start-up log ¶ A healthy start prints one row per step, with its time: 1 NVS OK ... 2 Comms OK ... 3 GPIO OK ... 4 Valves OK ... 5 ADC OK ... 6 LEDs OK ... 7 Temp OK ... Flux API initialized in ... ms FAIL marks a required step that failed, WARN a best-effort step that failed. Shutting down ¶ Flux::Shutdown() de-initialises the managers in reverse order (temperature, LEDs, ADC, GPIO, comms, NVS). Valves are not de-initialised by Shutdown() Flux::Shutdown() skips ValveManager (see the comment in Flux.cpp ). Disable the valve channels yourself ( flux.valves.DisableAllChannels() ) before shutting down.

docs.text: Ownership ¶ Who creates what, who owns it, and how long it lives. In one sentence: every manager is a function-local static singleton that lives for the whole program, and each manager creates and owns the handlers and bus objects it needs during its own initialisation. Managers, handlers and drivers Figure description and sources Managers on the left, hf-core handlers in the middle, chip drivers on the right. An arrow means "includes and uses": a manager owns the handler it points at, and each handler wraps exactly one driver. ValveManager owns both valve drivers (MAX22200 for the solenoid channels, TLE92466ED for the proportional channels), AdcManager owns the ADS7952 external ADC, and TemperatureManager owns the NTC and MCP9700 sensor handlers. LedManager uses its driver directly, without a handler. Managers with no arrow (communication buses, GPIO, NVS) talk to the interface wrap only. Drawn from: lib/managers #includes ; lib/core/handlers #includes ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/manager-dependencies.py . Manager map ¶ From the #include lines of lib/managers and the hf-core handlers; do not edit. Manager Uses managers hf-core handlers (driver) Drivers used directly Interface classes AdcManager CommChannelsManager ads7952 (hf-ads7952) - BaseAdc , EspAdc CommChannelsManager - - - BaseCan , BaseSpi , BaseUart , BaseUsbSerialJtag , EspCan , EspSpi , EspUart , EspUsbSerialJtag GpioManager - - - BaseGpio , EspGpio LedManager - - hf-ws2812-rmt - NvsManager - - - BaseNvs , EspNvs TemperatureManager AdcManager mcp9700 (hf-mcp9700), ntc (hf-ntc-thermistor) - BaseTemperature , EspTemperature ValveManager CommChannelsManager , GpioManager max22200 (hf-max22200), tle92466ed (hf-tle92466ed) - - Singletons ¶ Flux and every manager follow the same pattern: GetInstance() returns a function-local static object (constructed on first use; C++ guarantees that construction is thread-safe). docs.text: Threading ¶ What you can safely call from more than one FreeRTOS task. The HAL creates no tasks of its own : every call runs in the task that makes it, and periodic work (such as LED animations) is driven by your code. Locks ¶ Each manager has one RtosMutex (from hf-utils-rtos-wrap ). It is a recursive mutex, so a manager method that holds the lock may call another method of the same manager. Manager EnsureInitialized() Operations CommChannelsManager Locked (double-checked) AcquireUart() , GetSystemDiagnostics() and Deinitialize() lock; GetSpiDevice() , GetCanBus() , GetUart() and the USB serial accessors return pointers without locking NvsManager Not locked The BaseNvs objects do their own work; no manager-level lock GpioManager Locked (double-checked) Not locked : Set() , Read() , Toggle() and the other per-pin calls go straight to the pin ValveManager Locked (double-checked) Locked: every channel, configuration and fault call AdcManager Locked (double-checked) Locked: each read TemperatureManager Locked (double-checked) Locked: each read LedManager Locked (double-checked) Locked: colour, brightness and animation calls Flux facade Not locked Diagnostics read atomics Initialisation flags are std::atomic<bool> , read with acquire and written with release ordering. What that means for your code ¶ Initialise from one task. Flux::EnsureInitialized() and NvsManager::EnsureInitialized() have no lock; call Flux::EnsureInitialized() once from app_main() before you start other tasks. Valves, ADC, temperature and LED calls may be made from several tasks; the manager serialises them. A call can block while another task holds the manager's lock (for example during an SPI transfer). GPIO : give each pin one owner task, or add your own lock. Two tasks driving the same pin through GpioManager are not serialised, and the manager's operation counters are plain integers. Borrowed bus pointers ( GetSpiDevice() , GetCanBus() , AcquireUart() ) are shared objects. The valve drivers already use the valve SPI bus; if you talk to a device yourself, keep to one task per device. LED animations advance only when you call flux.leds.UpdateAnimation() ; call it from a periodic task (the animation step is 50 ms). CPU affinity ¶ FluxCpuAffinity.h names the logical cores your tasks should use on the dual-core ESP32-S3: flux_hal::kFluxCpuHostIo (0) for host, system and communication work and flux_hal::kFluxCpuRealtime (1) for high-rate loops such as pressure control. kFluxCpuNoAffinity (-1) lets the scheduler choose. Pass them to BaseThread or os_thread_create_pinned .

docs.text: Flux::EnsureInitialized() Figure description and sources Left to right, then the second row. The facade initialises the managers one at a time, in the order of the calls in its init function. The first group is required: if any of them fails, EnsureInitialized() returns false and the application should not continue. The second group is best effort: a failure there is logged as a warning, the manager stays unavailable and the system reports itself as degraded, so a bench with only some chips fitted still comes up. The order and the required / best-effort split are read from the init function, which returns false only in the required branches. docs.text: CommChannelsManager ¶ Owns the board's buses: the valve SPI bus (MAX22200 and TLE92466ED), the ADC SPI bus (ADS7952), the CAN controller, and up to three UARTs created on demand. Other managers borrow devices from it; application code rarely needs it except for CAN and UARTs. Source: CommChannelsManager.h . What it sets up ¶ Bus Pins (pin map names) Devices Settings Valve SPI (ESP-IDF SPI3_HOST ) SPI2_SCK , SPI2_MOSI , SPI2_MISO MAX22200_SOLENOID_DRIVER (CS SPI2_CS_MAX22200 ), TLE92466_LOWSIDE_DRIVER (CS SPI2_CS_TLE92466 ) Mode 0 and mode 1, both 1 MHz ADC SPI (ESP-IDF SPI2_HOST ) SPI3_SCK , SPI3_MOSI , SPI3_MISO ADS7952_ADC_0 (CS SPI3_CS_ADS7952_0 ) Mode 0, 4 MHz; only with HARDFOC_ADS7952_SUPPORT CAN (TWAI) TWAI_TX , TWAI_RX - 500 kbit/s UART 0-2 chosen by the caller e.g. the FDO2 probe on UART_FDO2_TX / UART_FDO2_RX Created by AcquireUart() GPIO numbers are on the pin map . There is no I2C bus on Flux V1. API ¶ Call Returns Notes GetSpiDevice(SpiDeviceId) BaseSpi* nullptr before initialisation or if the device failed to attach GetCanBus() BaseCan* nullptr if CAN failed to start AcquireUart(const UartAcquireConfig&) BaseUart* First call for a port creates and caches it; later calls return the cached port and ignore the new config. rts_pin >= 0 enables RS-485 half-duplex GetUart(port) BaseUart* The cached port, or nullptr AcquireUsbSerialJtag(cfg) , GetUsbSerialJtag() BaseUsbSerialJtag* The USB serial / JTAG peripheral; returns nullptr because HF_CORE_ENABLE_USB_SERIAL_JTAG is off in this HAL's CMakeLists.txt GetI2cBus() EspI2cBus* Always nullptr on Flux V1 GetLastError() , GetSystemDiagnostics(CommSystemDiagnostics&) , DumpStatistics() See below Example: open a UART for a sensor ¶ #include "api/Flux.h" #include "managers/CommChannelsManager.h" CommChannelsManager :: UartAcquireConfig cfg {}; cfg . port_number = 1 ; cfg . tx_pin = 47 ; // UART_FDO2_TX on the pin map cfg . rx_pin = 48 ; // UART_FDO2_RX cfg . rts_pin = -1 ; // plain UART (no RS-485 direction pin) cfg . cts_pin = -1 ; cfg . baud_bps = 19200 ; cfg . tx_buffer_size = 256 ; cfg . rx_buffer_size = 256 ; BaseUart * uart = Flux :: GetInstance (). comms . AcquireUart ( cfg ); if ( uart == nullptr ) { // port out of range or the UART failed to start: see the log } Read the pin numbers from the pin map in real code ( GetGpioMapping(HfFunctionalGpioPin::UART_FDO2_TX) ) rather than writing them down. Diagnostics ¶ GetSystemDiagnostics() fills CommSystemDiagnostics : spi_bus_valid , can_bus_valid , spi_device_count and the last CommError . i2c_bus_valid is always false. DumpStatistics() logs the bus states. Pitfalls ¶ Names versus hosts. SPI2_* pins are the ESP-IDF SPI3_HOST , SPI3_* pins are SPI2_HOST (see Hardware ). Sharing a device. The valve drivers already use their SPI devices through ValveManager . Talking to them directly through GetSpiDevice() bypasses ValveManager 's lock and channel state. UART port 0 is normally the ESP-IDF console. Pick a free port. First AcquireUart() wins. A second call for the same port with a different baud rate silently gets the first configuration (the header comment promises a warning; the code does not log one).

docs.text: GpioManager ¶ Creates one ESP32 GPIO object for every GPIO -category pin of the pin map and lets you drive or read it by name or by enum. On Flux V1 those are the control and fault lines of the two valve drivers. Source: GpioManager.h . Which pins it owns ¶ At start-up it walks the pin map and registers each pin whose category is GPIO (or user) and whose chip is the ESP32. Core pins (boot, USB) and comm pins (SPI, CAN, UART, LED data) are skipped; their owners configure them. The names are the Name column of the pin map : GPIO_MAX22200_ENABLE , GPIO_MAX22200_CMD , GPIO_MAX22200_FAULT_N , GPIO_MAX22200_TRIGA , GPIO_MAX22200_TRIGB , GPIO_TLE92466_EN , GPIO_TLE92466_RESN , GPIO_TLE92466_DRV0 , GPIO_TLE92466_DRV1 , GPIO_TLE92466_FAULT_N . Each pin gets its polarity, pull and drive from the pin map. "Active" means the pin's asserted level, so for an active-low pin SetActive() drives it low. API ¶ Call Notes Get(std::string_view name) , Get(HfFunctionalGpioPin pin) BaseGpio* , or nullptr if not registered Set(name, bool active) , SetActive(name) , SetInactive(name) , Toggle(name) Return hf_gpio_err_t Read(name, bool& active) , IsActive(name, bool& active) Logical state (polarity applied) SetDirection , SetPullMode , SetOutputMode Reconfigure a pin at run time ConfigureInterrupt(name, trigger, callback, user_data) , EnableInterrupt , DisableInterrupt , SupportsInterrupts Edge interrupts on a registered pin Contains(name) , Size() Lookup helpers GetLastError() , GetSystemDiagnostics(GpioSystemDiagnostics&) , DumpStatistics() Operation counters and the last error Example: watch a fault line ¶ #include "api/Flux.h" #include "managers/GpioManager.h" auto & gpio = Flux :: GetInstance (). gpio ; bool fault = false ; if ( gpio . Read ( "GPIO_TLE92466_FAULT_N" , fault ) == hf_gpio_err_t :: GPIO_SUCCESS && fault ) { // the TLE92466ED is asserting its fault output (pin is active low; Read() returns "active") } Prefer the enum form ( gpio.Get(HfFunctionalGpioPin::TLE92466_FAULT_N) ) in loops: the string form searches the table on every call. Diagnostics ¶ GetSystemDiagnostics() reports the number of registered pins and the total, successful and failed operation counts. DumpStatistics() logs the same and the per-pin access and error counts. Pitfalls ¶ Every pin starts as an output. Registration configures all pins as outputs, including the _FAULT_N inputs. ValveManager switches the two fault pins to inputs during its own start-up; if you use a pin as an input before that, call SetDirection(name, HF_GPIO_DIRECTION_INPUT) first. The valve drivers own their control pins. Changing GPIO_TLE92466_EN or GPIO_MAX22200_ENABLE behind ValveManager 's back disables outputs it thinks are on. No lock on pin operations. See Threading . A wrong name returns GPIO_ERR_PIN_NOT_FOUND , not a crash. Copy names from the pin map.

docs.text: NvsManager ¶ Gives the application three separate key-value stores in the ESP32's NVS flash partition, so calibration data, configuration and ordinary application data never collide. Source: NvsManager.h . Accessor NVS namespace Use it for App() flux Counters, last state, anything the application owns Calibration() flux_cal Factory or bench calibration Config() flux_cfg User or deployment configuration Each accessor returns a BaseNvs& (the interface class; the ESP32 implementation is EspNvs ). API ¶ Call Notes App() , Calibration() , Config() BaseNvs& for the namespace BaseNvs::SetU32 / GetU32 , SetString / GetString , SetBlob / GetBlob Return hf_nvs_err_t ; the ESP32 implementation commits each write BaseNvs::KeyExists , EraseKey , GetSize , Commit EnsureInitialized() , IsInitialized() , Deinitialize() Opens / closes all three namespaces GetLastError() , DumpStatistics() DumpStatistics() logs each namespace and whether it is open Example: a boot counter ¶ #include "api/Flux.h" #include "managers/NvsManager.h" auto & flux = Flux :: GetInstance (); if ( flux . EnsureInitialized ()) { BaseNvs & app = flux . nvs . App (); hf_u32_t boots = 0 ; if ( app . GetU32 ( "boot_cnt" , boots ) != hf_nvs_err_t :: NVS_SUCCESS ) { boots = 0 ; // first boot, or the key was erased } ( void ) app . SetU32 ( "boot_cnt" , boots + 1 ); } The flux_nvs_example app shows strings and blobs in all three namespaces. Pitfalls ¶ Key length. ESP-IDF NVS keys are at most 15 characters ( GetMaxKeyLength() ). GetLastError() only reflects initialisation; check each BaseNvs call's return value. No lock on initialisation. Let Flux::EnsureInitialized() open NVS from one task before others use it.

docs.text: TemperatureManager ¶ Reads the board's three temperature sensors by name and keeps simple statistics. Source: TemperatureManager.h . Name Sensor Read through ESP32_INTERNAL The ESP32-S3's internal temperature sensor EspTemperature NTC_THERMISTOR 10 kΩ NTC, B = 3950, 10 kΩ series resistor, 3.3 V AdcManager channel ESP32_NTC_THERMISTOR MCP9700_THERMISTOR MCP9700 analog sensor AdcManager channel ADS7952_0_CH8 (needs HARDFOC_MCP9700_SUPPORT and a working ADS7952) The manager starts if at least one sensor works; the others are left out and reads of them return SENSOR_NOT_FOUND . API ¶ Call Notes ReadTemperatureCelsius(name, float&) , ReadTemperatureFahrenheit(name, float&) By name ReadInternalTemperature(float&) , ReadNtcTemperature(float&) , ReadMcp9700Temperature(float&) Shortcuts for the three names GetSystemTemperatureStats(min, max, avg) Reads every registered sensor and summarises GetSensorCount() , GetSensorEntry(name) Registered sensors; TempEntry keeps the last reading and counters GetLastError() , GetSystemDiagnostics(TempSystemDiagnostics&) , DumpStatistics() Example: board temperature with a fallback ¶ #include "api/Flux.h" #include "managers/TemperatureManager.h" auto & temp = Flux :: GetInstance (). temp ; float c = 0.0f ; if ( temp . ReadNtcTemperature ( c ) != TemperatureError :: SUCCESS ) { ( void ) temp . ReadInternalTemperature ( c ); // the die sensor runs warmer than the board } Diagnostics ¶ GetSystemDiagnostics() gives registered sensors, operation counters, and the minimum, maximum and average of the last readings. DumpStatistics() logs each sensor's last value and counters. Pitfalls ¶ Start-up order matters. The thermistors depend on AdcManager ; if the ADC failed, only ESP32_INTERNAL registers. The internal sensor measures the chip , not the valves or the board; it reads higher than ambient. NTC values are fixed in code (B, series resistor, reference voltage). A different thermistor means changing TemperatureManager.cpp .

docs.text: ValveManager ¶ The reason the board exists. One API for fourteen valve channels on two different driver chips: eight on/off solenoid channels on the MAX22200 and six proportional channels on the TLE92466ED. Source: ValveManager.h . Channels ¶ ValveChannel Chip Hardware channel Control SOL_CH0 ... SOL_CH7 MAX22200 0-7 On / off with a hit phase and a hold phase, set by current (CDR) or by duty (VDR) PROP_CH0 ... PROP_CH5 TLE92466ED 0-5 Regulated coil current in mA, with PWM frequency and dither The table is kValveChannelMap in the header; FindChannel("SOL_CH3") turns a name into a channel. API ¶ Call Channels Notes EnableChannel(ch) , DisableChannel(ch) all Switch one output EnableChannelsMask(uint16_t mask) all Bits 0-7 solenoids, bits 8-13 proportional DisableAllChannels() all IsChannelEnabled(ch) all From the manager's channel state ConfigureSolenoidCdr(ch, hit_ma, hold_ma, hit_time_ms) solenoid Current drive: hit current, hold current, hit time ConfigureSolenoidVdr(ch, hit_duty_pct, hold_duty_pct, hit_time_ms) solenoid Voltage (duty) drive SetProportionalCurrent(ch, current_ma) proportional Set-point of the current regulator ConfigureProportionalPwm(ch, frequency_hz) proportional Must be > 0 ConfigureProportionalDither(ch, amplitude_ma, frequency_hz) proportional Small oscillation that reduces valve stiction HasFault() , HasSolenoidFault() , HasProportionalFault() , ClearAllFaults() GetSolenoidFaults(max22200::FaultStatus&) , GetProportionalFaults(tle92466ed::FaultReport&) Chip-level fault detail GetChannelState(ch) all ValveChannelState : enabled, configured, current, duty, PWM, dither, counters GetMax22200Handler() , GetTle92466Handler() The handlers, for chip features not wrapped here ( nullptr if that chip failed) All of them return hf_valve_err_t (or bool ); calling a solenoid-only call on a proportional channel returns VALVE_ERR_CHANNEL_TYPE_MISMATCH . Example: one solenoid and one proportional valve ¶ #include "api/Flux.h" #include "esp_log.h" #include "managers/ValveManager.h" auto & flux = Flux :: GetInstance (); if ( flux . EnsureInitialized () && flux . valves . IsInitialized ()) { auto & valves = flux . valves ; // Solenoid: 800 mA for 50 ms to pull in, then hold at 200 mA. hf_valve_err_t err = valves . ConfigureSolenoidCdr ( ValveChannel :: SOL_CH0 , 800 , 200 , 50.0f ); if ( HfValveErrOk ( err )) { err = valves . EnableChannel ( ValveChannel :: SOL_CH0 ); } // Proportional: 200 Hz PWM, 400 mA set-point. ( void ) valves . ConfigureProportionalPwm ( ValveChannel :: PROP_CH0 , 200.0f ); if ( HfValveErrOk ( valves . EnableChannel ( ValveChannel :: PROP_CH0 ))) { ( void ) valves . SetProportionalCurrent ( ValveChannel :: PROP_CH0 , 400 ); } if ( ! HfValveErrOk ( err )) { ESP_LOGE ( "app" , "valve: %s" , HfValveErrToString ( err )); } } The valve_manager_example and valve_cycling_test apps go further. What start-up does ¶ EnsureInitialized() brings up comms and GPIO, then tries each chip on its own, so one missing chip never blocks the other: TLE92466ED : creates the handler, enters mission mode, drives its enable pin, clears the feedback freeze so the per-channel feedback registers update, and sets the supply under- / over-voltage trips to 19 V / 29 V for the 24 V valve rail. MAX22200 : creates the handler with a 15 kΩ reference resistor (full-scale current 1000 mA). It succeeds if either chip works and logs which one is missing. Use GetSystemDiagnostics() to see max22200_initialized and tle92466_initialized . Diagnostics ¶ GetSystemDiagnostics(ValveSystemDiagnostics&) : which chips are up, configured and active channels, total activations and errors. GetChannelState(ch) gives per-channel counters. DumpStatistics() logs both. Pitfalls ¶ Configure, then enable. A solenoid enabled before ConfigureSolenoidCdr/Vdr runs with whatever its channel registers hold. Currents are limited by the chip setup. The MAX22200 full scale is 1000 mA with this board's reference resistor; a set-point above it cannot be reached. GetLastError() is not updated. Use each call's return value (see Errors ). Flux::Shutdown() does not turn valves off. Call DisableAllChannels() first. Valve supply off looks like a working chip on SPI with no coil current. Check the 24 V rail and GetProportionalFaults() (the TLE92466ED reports supply under-voltage).
